comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA curriculum, checked 2026-09-29, defines one complete 180-EC Medicine pathway with 60 EC in each year and no formal route. Year 1 combines four patient-centred organ-system themes, a 6-EC observation and care placement, clinical and scientific methodology, academic formation and professional development. Year 2 deepens the same themes and longitudinal formation while preserving 18 EC of genuine elective space. Year 3 continues the themes and formation, includes a 12-EC medical bachelor thesis and culminates in a 14-EC preparation-for-practice block focused on clinical reasoning, history-taking and physical examination before clerkships. The official overview confirms the normalized identity, three-year 180-EC load, Dutch language, Amsterdam UMC location and RIO code 56551. Elective space is preserved without invented content.
components: Patient-centred theme covering pregnancy, birth, and physical and sexual development.

Patient-centred theme covering metabolic, hormonal and immunological regulation.
Patient-centred theme covering cardiovascular, pulmonary and renal systems.

Patient-centred study of arrhythmia, coagulation disorders, pulmonary embolism and renal failure.

Patient-centred study of complex orthopaedics, central functional disorders and psychiatric disorders.
Human development from embryo through older age, with population health, the older patient and the health-care system.
Final bachelor block preparing for medical clerkships, centred on clinical reasoning and assessment of physical examination and history-taking skills.

exception.reason: The UvA Medicine bachelor is an integrated, patient-centred medical programme. Four recurring organ-system themes are taught through disease cases; clinical lectures include real patients from the first year; students complete a compulsory observation and care placement; and medical-technical and medical-communication skills, history-taking, physical examination, clinical reasoning, academic formation and professional development progress across all three years. The 14-EC final practice block explicitly prepares students for medical clerkships. UCR can build a strong biomedical and health-sciences programme, but it cannot reproduce the compulsory patient-facing placement, longitudinal clinical-skills training, supervised medical communication and examination, integrated diagnostic reasoning or medical professional formation. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be biomedical science with psychology and public health, not a defensible Medicine programme.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official curriculum accounts for all 180 EC as three 60-EC years. Year 1 has 40 EC of four patient-centred organ-system themes, a 6-EC observation and care placement, 6 EC of clinical and scientific methodology, 5 EC of academic formation and 3 EC of professional development. Year 2 has 30 EC of repeated and deepened themes, 4 EC of academic formation, 3 EC of professional development and 18 EC of genuine elective space. Year 3 has 25 EC of further organ-system themes, a 12-EC medically focused bachelor thesis, a 14-EC preparation-for-practice block, 6 EC of academic formation and 3 EC of professional development. No formal route is selected and the elective space remains open.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide substantial life-science foundations. HCBBIOM211 Functional Anatomy, HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease provide advanced biomedical content. HCBGATE102 Introduction to Brain & Behavior, HCBCOGN112 Neurobiology and UCR psychology courses cover brain, behaviour and mental-health perspectives; HCBBIOM111 Epidemiology & Public Health and ethics, sociology, communication and research-methods courses add population, societal, ethical and scientific perspectives. The workbook nevertheless contains no patient-facing clinical placement, no history-taking or physical-examination course, no longitudinal medical-technical and medical-communication skills strand, no integrated diagnostic-reasoning progression, no supervised medical professional-development curriculum, and no preparation for clinical clerkships. These compulsory programme-wide clinical gaps cannot be repaired by selecting adjacent biomedical, psychology, public-health or communication courses.
